text:
anya: brain-dump from today's sync: propose we combine the hierarchical quota shim (admission + edge soft-cap) with 'escrowed bursts' + probe-based topups. sketching the interoperable flow so we can decide which pieces to RFC next.

maria.k: love the combo. main concern is complexity + operator mental load. TL;DR what changes at the edge vs admission?

anya: edges keep local escrow counters (tiny, per-tenant). when escrow hits threshold they either consult cached admission decision (fast) or send a cheap probe to admission. admission still enforces the global safety_bound and emits signed decision_tokens or a numeric abuse_score. edges use either path: token => immediate topup, high abuse_score => aggressive soft-shed, neither => local degrade.

kevin: probe payload? want as small as possible to avoid adding tail cost.

anya: minimal: { tenant_id, escrow_left, probe_nonce, recent_local_429s }. response: { allow_topup, topup_amount, decision_token, abuse_score }. compact ints + short token. goal: <200 bytes.

priya: telemetry implications? counts and small histograms per tenant. how much storage + cost?

anya: keep TTL short (5-15m raw, 1h rollups). admission aggregates on the fly; offline rollups for trend. initial cost estimate: ~0.2 CPU per 100k tenants and modest egress.

samir: abuse detection — heuristic vs classifier? earlier thread used simple rules. do you propose both?

anya: start heuristic-first for safety: retry density, 95/50 latency gap, 429 velocity. Add a lightweight classifier later if heuristics hit wall. classifier only used to veto topups, not to deny baseline traffic. Always require >=2 signals before a hard ban.

maria.k: how do we avoid clients fanout-ing to many edges to bypass admission?

kevin: admission global escrow accounting plus decision_tokens that include a nonce + region tag. admission caps total topups per tenant per refill-window. edges can be limited by token signature and short TTL so spreading yields diminishing returns.

priya: refill-window defaults?

anya: defaults: refill every 10s, per-tenant global escrow budget = min( commit*0.05, 500 ). shards get per-shard floor so one noisy shard can't starve others. Configurable per-customer.

samir: rollout plan? what do we flip when?

anya: staged: 1) offline sim with historical traces across shards. 2) shadow probes + shadow abuse scoring for 2w. 3) enable probe->topup for 1% tenants (non-critical). 4) increase with metrics gates (client 429 down, p99 latency unchanged, FP under threshold). 5) enable signed decision_token-driven soft-shed adjustments. Full global enforcement only after 90-day bake.

maria.k: operator controls? need per-tenant emergency revoke and quick rollback.

anya: decision_tokens stored in admission log + admin revoke endpoint. Edges poll revocation list every 30s and can fallback to local-only policy. Also plan a kill-switch flag central control can set.

kevin: proto design: want a tiny v1 proto for probes and a v1 for decisions. will send draft. batch probes for hot tenants every 25ms to reduce RPCs.

priya: SLOs / dashboards to watch: probe latency, topup success ratio, per-tenant escrow hit rate, abuse_score distribution, FP incidents (benign bursts throttled). We'll need per-customer alerts for PLG churn risk.

samir: Dedicated/private: Dedicated gets a local admission daemon that can operate standalone and sync log to central control-plane for global metrics. Private deployment can opt-in to central abuse signals or run fully offline; doc tradeoffs clearly.

maria.k: security: decision_tokens must be HMAC-signed and include expiry + shard salt. Edges validate signature and TTL. No client-facing surface for abuse_score.

kevin: testing: load replay, synthetic fanout attacks, and per-tenant chaos tests. also fuzz the decision_token path to ensure edges reject malformed tokens.

anya: infra changes: small escrow ledger service (ephemeral), admission caching layer, token-bank read API tweak to return committed budget + reserve hints. Low-risk storage additions.

priya: any alternative simpler approach we should keep on the table?

maria.k: simpler fallback is global abuse_score broadcast + edge-only soft-cap. cheaper but harsher for benign bursts. Use combo if retention cost of false 429s is high.

anya: next step: I'll write combined follow-up RFC w/ proto sketches, rollout checklist, sim metrics, operator playbook, and a minimal set of dashboards. aiming EOD Weds. volunteers to review?

kevin: I'll review proto + batching.

priya: I'll draft dashboard queries and FP alert thresholds.

samir: I'll help with simulation harness and Dedicated daemon plan.

maria.k: thanks all. @deploy-bot please post RFC when ready. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: RFC draft published: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/1798765432-escrow-probe-hybrid-hierarchical-shim (permissions: eng-infra, eng-platform)

priya: ack, reading now.

kevin: will start proto PR tomorrow.
